content.body:
The Swedish-designed Bofors 40 mm found wide acceptance around the world, and could be found in the inventories of both Allied and Axis powers. Clip-fed, it could keep up an impressive rate of fire without stopping for reloads.
In Battleground Europe, the Bofors is an exceptional general purpose weapon against either ground or aerial targets.
The commander (crew position 1) has 2-stage magnification for target acquisition as well as a crosshair and rangefinder. The gunner (crew position 2) looks through the open ring sight. This sight is particularly useful against fast-moving air targets but the lack of a magnified gunner's sight is particularly noticed when trying to engage ground targets at range, especially if they are somewhat camouflaged.
When using the Bofors against aircraft, be aggressive. You have an ample ammunition supply, no reloading delay, and a flat trajectory making it effective with little bullet drop all the way out to 2 km. If that enemy aircraft has a grey circle forming around it, fire away! The slew rate for the 360 degree gun platform is very fast, you can engage and track close-flying aircraft without too much difficulty.
Against ground targets, you will notice that the dispersion of the relatively lightweight 40 mm HE shells is fairly high, and you will likely have to walk your fire across your target. 40 mm HE doesn't penetrate armor particularly well, but explosive effects will jar any target making it nearly impossible for them to successfully fire back at you.
As a heavy gun, the Bofors can be manhandled albeit slowly. It is better to get a prime mover to pull you to a location with clear fields of fire in all directions. A very good location is on the steep side of a hill, just below the crest. Being below the crest will keep you from skylining (your silhouette being obvious because it sticks up into the skyline), reduce the arc of sky you need to cover to about 180 degrees, and, if attacked by infantry or otherwise under pressure, you can simply undeploy the gun and quickly roll down hill.
Keep in mind that you have no gun shield, so you are particularly vulnerable to a lone sniper.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
